QF.id: AIF Valuation Taxation and Good Practices_65

answer.text: Protecting client/investor confidential data, using it only for authorized purposes, and implementing adequate security controls and a confidentiality policy

explanation.text: The Logic: Per NISM XIX-A (pp. 271-272, 277), distributors must maintain absolute data privacy for confidential and proprietary investor and investment-manager data, implement adequate internal controls and encryption/security measures, allow disclosure only when authorised, and adopt a confidentiality policy that binds employees. The Trap: Free sharing or publication of investor data breaches both the distributor agreement and the workbook's good-practice standards, even if no statutory complaint follows. Note: Treat investor data — and information about the investment manager — as confidential by default; written authorisation should be the trigger for any disclosure beyond the routine fund-operations workflow.
